answer: An agent economy resists sybils by running random walks on the identity trust graph. Honest agents form a densely connected grove; a fake cluster is a mirror of puppets dangling from a few attack edges. A detection kernel computes each node's walk landing probability from a trusted seed: frequent landings mark honest members, while puppets reachable only through a sparse bottleneck score near zero and are excluded from voting and emissions. Cost: forging reciprocal trust edges and dense fake structure scales with cluster size squared, far above the near-free minting of bare identities.
